title: Bulkhead Pattern
description: Learn the bulkhead pattern to isolate failures and prevent resource exhaustion.

data.text: The bulkhead pattern, named after ship compartments, isolates failures to prevent them from affecting the entire system. Amazon and Netflix use bulkheads to ensure that a failure in one service does not exhaust resources needed by other services.

Bulkheads partition resources like thread pools, connection pools, and memory into isolated compartments. If one compartment fails, the others remain functional. This prevents a single failing service from consuming all available resources.

data.title: Bulkhead Isolation Strategies
items: Thread pool isolation: Separate thread pools for different downstream services
Connection pool isolation: Separate database or HTTP connection pools
Semaphore isolation: Limit concurrent calls to a service
Process isolation: Run critical services in separate processes

data.title: Netflix Hystrix Bulkhead
data.text: Netflix Hystrix uses thread pool isolation by default. Each downstream service gets its own thread pool. If the payment service is slow, its thread pool fills up, but the user service thread pool remains healthy.

data.title: Example: Thread Pool Bulkhead
data.code: Separate thread pools for different downstream services.

# Without bulkhead: One shared thread pool
# If Payment Service is slow, all calls share the same pool
# Result: Order, User, and Inventory calls also slow down

# With bulkhead: Separate thread pools
# Order Service calls -> Thread Pool A (10 threads)
# Payment Service calls -> Thread Pool B (5 threads)
# Inventory Service calls -> Thread Pool C (10 threads)

# If Payment Service is slow:
# Thread Pool B fills up
# Thread Pool A and C remain healthy
# Orders and inventory operations continue normally

items.question: What is the difference between bulkhead and circuit breaker?
items.answer: Bulkhead prevents resource exhaustion by isolating resources. Circuit breaker stops calling a failing service. They are complementary; use both for maximum resilience.

items.question: How many threads per pool?
items.answer: Depends on your workload. Start with 10-50 threads per pool and adjust based on latency and throughput. More threads increase concurrency but also context switching overhead.

items.question: Should I use semaphore or thread pool isolation?
items.answer: Thread pool isolation is safer but has more overhead. Semaphore isolation is lighter but shares threads. Use thread pools for I/O-heavy services and semaphores for CPU-heavy services.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Bulkheads isolate failures to prevent cascading effects
Use separate thread pools for different downstream services
Complementary to circuit breakers and timeouts
Choose thread pool or semaphore based on workload
data.takeaway: Bulkheads ensure that one failing service does not bring down your entire system.
